title: The first ship
text: A merchant brig {~is hull-down on the horizon|has run up her colours and nothing else|is sitting heavy and low in the water}. Your crew is watching you, not her.

outcomes.text: It was loud and quick and I didn't hear any of it afterwards. We took her with two wounded and a ship's cat.
The brig's crew fought harder than their cargo deserved. We won, but I counted names that evening.

choices.label: Fire a warning gun and let her surrender

outcomes.text: She struck her colours at once. The captain handed over the manifest with a face I'll remember.
She ran, and we lost the wind and the day. The crew called it cowardice, quietly.
The crew muttered. At dusk the lookout spotted a warship on her course, and I was thanked in a way I didn't expect.
It was the right call and the crew never forgave it. A week later someone left a rope in my cabin.

title: The poster
text: In {~a harbour you haven't touched in a year|a port you thought you'd never need|a tavern nobody should have recognised you in}, there is a poster with {~your face on it, drawn by someone who'd only heard about you|a price, a description and a spelling of your name that's almost right}.

choices.label: Laugh and keep your hat low

outcomes.text: It became a joke aboard. They drew moustaches on the copies we stole.
A boy recognised me and followed us to the quay. I paid him to forget, and he took the money.
I went from wall to wall in the dark. By morning there wasn't a poster in the port. Nobody asked who.
I was spotted at the third wall. We left that port in a hurry and never went back.
I sent them a better portrait. The poster has been redrawn with a flattering profile, and the bounty rose to match.
The new poster flattered my enemies more than me, and the bounty rose for a reason I didn't want.

title: The map
text: The second map {~is stained with something you decide not to identify|has a corner torn off and an X in the wrong ocean|is the first one that isn't a fake}. Your quartermaster has opinions about it.

outcomes.text: We found the island, and the chest, and a better reason to come back. It paid for the ship twice.
The island was real. So was the guard somebody had left on it. We left with a third of the chest and a limp.

choices.label: Sell it to the highest bidder

outcomes.text: A rival paid in gold, and we spent three months wondering if it was the right call.
The buyer disappeared with the map and a few of our best sailors. A bad bargain.
It felt like freedom for about an hour. Then the crew noticed what I'd done.
The ash on the water looked like a very small continent. We sailed on and nobody mentioned it again.

title: A captain's table
text: You're invited to {~dine with the other captains|a meeting of ships|a truce in a harbour with no flag}. {~Three of them have wanted you dead.|Everyone brought their best manners.}

outcomes.text: Three of them left owing me favours. One of them meant it.
It was a trap, but a polite one: they wanted a share, and I paid it.
It was tense and short. Nobody said what they wanted, and everyone remembered I'd come.
A glass was thrown and a pistol drawn. We left with a duel pending and a good story.

choices.label: Send a crewmate in your place

outcomes.text: They handled it better than I would have. I was reminded who had my back.
They were insulted by an empty chair. It took a gift to apologise.

title: What the song says
text: The song {~about your ship|that the harbours sing|that a stranger started singing in a tavern} has a verse that isn't true. {~It's the best verse.|Everyone knows it by heart.}

outcomes.text: A legend is built out of better material than facts. I let it grow.
A younger crew tried to live up to the verse. Two of them died doing it.
I told the true story at the next port. It was less popular and more memorable.
Nobody wanted the real version. They rewrote the verse with my correction as the joke.
I wrote the next verse and it stuck. That's the kind of immortality you can plan for.
The new verse was awful and everyone sang it anyway.

title: The first winter under glass
text: The seals on {~Hab Three|the east corridor|the greenhouse airlock} are failing at the worst moment. Engineers argue with each other in three languages.

outcomes.text: Six hours in a suit, and the seal held. They stopped arguing and started thanking me.
The patch held for a day. Then it didn't. The proper repair took a week and a crew of eight.
I kept eight people on task and nobody got hurt. It isn't glamorous and it was right.
The decision I made cost us a night of air. We got through it, and I learned where my limits were.
We moved forty people into the dome in an hour. Nobody died. The module was lost.
Panic cost us more than the leak would have. Someone was hurt in the stairwell.

title: Something out there
text: On the survey, {~a regular pattern in the rock|a pale line that isn't geology|a radio hush that's too regular} shows up on the {~third|fourth|fifth} pass. You are the only one who has looked at it for long.

outcomes.text: The council gave it a number and a team. The team gave it a name. It was mine.
It was dismissed as noise. A year later someone else reported the same thing and was believed.
Three more months of data and I had something no one could dismiss.
The more I looked the less I could tell anyone. I was starting to seem odd.
It was noise. I slept well and was almost disappointed.
It wasn't noise. I'd find that out when it was too late to be first.

title: The vote
text: The council is deciding whether to {~spend a season's rations on a new dome|let the greenhouse take the water|send an expedition to the north pole}. The vote is tied. Everyone is looking at you.

outcomes.text: The dome went up. It stood for a century. I was remembered for the decision, which pleased me.
The dome was late, over budget and cold. People forgave it eventually.
We kept our reserves. The next dust storm lasted forty days and justified every ration.
The reserves rotted in a bad store. I stood by the vote and it cost me.
The chair broke the tie. I was irrelevant, which is its own kind of clarity.
The chair broke the tie in a way I'd have voted against. I'd given up the right to complain.

title: The reply
text: {~The signal changes|A second signal arrives on the same frequency|The pattern repeats, and then isn't quite the same}. It is, depending on how you squint, an answer.

outcomes.text: The next answer came in nine hours. Whatever it was, it was listening.
We sent something clumsy. The reply was silence, and it has lasted.
Earth took eleven minutes to reply and then a long time to decide. We were told to wait.
The report leaked, and the colony learned about it from the news feed. I wasn't thanked.
I listened for a year. The pattern changed three times, each time more patient.
Someone else noticed what I was hiding. The conversation we had was not a pleasant one.

title: The founders' wall
text: They are putting names on the {~wall in the central hall|plaque by the first airlock|stone by the greenhouse}. Yours is being discussed.

choices.label: Stand back and let them decide

outcomes.text: They put it up. A child touched it later and asked what a founder was.
They argued for a year and put it up, smaller than I'd have liked.

choices.label: Ask for a name beside yours

outcomes.text: I put up the name of the first man who died building the colony. It still has fresh flowers.
They agreed, and the other names were tricky. It turned into an argument I regretted starting.
They put the name up anyway. It's what the colony wanted, and in the end I let it.
They left it off. For a few months I liked it that way.

title: A shopkeeper who stares
text: {~A shopkeeper|A landlady|A policeman} has been looking at you for a while. {~Your coat is almost right.|You said a word you shouldn't have.|You paid with coins that were slightly too clean.}

outcomes.text: They helped me, then told the whole street about the foreigner who was lost. Everyone was kind.
It worked, and I spent the evening composing a better story.
I walked out quickly and the shopkeeper wasn't sure. I never went back.
I walked into the wrong street, and into someone I owed a story.
I said I was from abroad and a little unwell. It explained everything and I became a minor local mystery.
They believed it too much, and offered to find me a wife, a job and a doctor.

title: The first jump
text: The device is {~warm|humming|reading a number you've never seen}. You can go to {~a year you know from a book|a day you will regret leaving|somewhere you can't possibly return from}.

outcomes.text: A few years. The world looked the same and wasn't. It was the quietest kind of vertigo.
It went wrong in a small way: I landed in a field, three days off. I was found by a farmer.

choices.label: Jump to a day you remember

outcomes.text: I saw someone I loved, from across a street, alive, unaware. I did not speak.
I did speak. They looked at me the way you look at a stranger, and then at my coat.
I put the device in a drawer. It hummed in the drawer for a week.
I sat with it all night. In the morning I knew I'd do it eventually.

title: The collection
text: A museum {~curator|collector|professor} has noticed the artifacts you document. {~They'd like to see the originals.|They've found a mistake in your catalogue.|They want to buy one.}

outcomes.text: They wept at the sight of a single button. We became friends, and neither of us said why.
They saw something I hadn't. It was a gift, and it was a danger.
The price was ridiculous and the buyer was thrilled. I felt oddly clean.
It was the wrong one. The buyer asked questions I couldn't answer.
They never asked again. I was sorry about that.
They left it, and I discovered I'd sent a signal anyway.

title: The tear
text: A thing you did {~in 1920|last week|somewhere you don't remember} is {~showing up in the wrong newspaper|visible in a photograph where it shouldn't be}. The timeline has noticed.

outcomes.text: It took three attempts, and left a scar on the date. But it held.
I made it worse. The photograph changed, and so did the person in it.
History absorbed it. It always does, a little more than you'd think.
History did not absorb it. A small, specific thing was different the next morning.
It was an act of aggression against time. Time shrugged.
It was a catastrophe, and a very educational one.

title: Which year is home?
text: Somebody asks you where you're from. For the first time you {~don't know what to say|have a real answer|say a year}.

choices.label: Name the year you were born

outcomes.text: It felt like a lie and a truth. I hadn't been that person for a very long time.
It felt like a country I'd left. The person asking nodded as if they understood.
It's the right answer for a life. I felt like a person for the first time in a long time.
It was more honest than I'd expected. They told me the date, and I nodded.
They laughed. 'Of course.' They've decided it's a joke, and I let it be one.
They went quiet. I'd said too much by not saying it.

title: A place in the line
text: At dinner, {~someone says the word 'heir' and the table goes quiet|a courtier uses your title for the first time|you realise you've been placed in the order, and you're not first}. {~You can feel everyone counting.|The soup goes cold.}

outcomes.text: It was easier than I'd feared. A cousin nodded, which meant something.
I overdid the grace and was taken for ambition. It took a year to live down.

choices.label: Ask what it means in practice

outcomes.text: The answer was a stack of binders and a personal secretary. I felt rather important and slightly ill.
The courtier laughed and I was handed a diary. Every day for two years had an engagement in it.
It was quietly noted. My mother did not speak to me for a week, then did.
It was reported in the papers. The palace denied it, and everyone knew.

title: The first decree
text: A document is placed in front of you with {~a ribbon|a pen|a nervous clerk}. {~It's a small matter: a holiday, a street, a name.|It's about a hospital, and you suspect it's about more than that.}

outcomes.text: My first act as a decree-maker went into history as a footnote. A hospital got a new wing.
It had a clause I hadn't read. The clause was used against someone I liked.
The clerk rewrote it with a look of dread. It came out better. I was told I had a gift for the work.
The rewrite offended a minister. I'd made an enemy and a draft.

choices.label: Ask for a week to think

outcomes.text: A week was too long for politics and exactly right for conscience. I signed on the eighth day.
The week ran out the decision for me. Someone else had signed in my name.

title: The crown
text: The {~cathedral|abbey|great hall} is full. Someone is holding the crown with both hands, as if it might say something. You know every {~face|name} in the room.

choices.label: Take it with a steady hand

outcomes.text: My hands were steady. My voice wasn't. The country forgave the second.
I took it and meant every word of the oath. Later I would regret how literally I'd meant it.

choices.label: Add a line to the oath

outcomes.text: I added a sentence about the poor. It was reported with wonder and quoted for decades.
The archbishop did not know what to do. We stopped, and the whole country watched me explain.
The crowd wept with me. For a day we were one country.
The papers said I looked unfit. The week after, the polls said the opposite.

title: Ten years in
text: A decade on the throne is marked by {~a parade|a state dinner|a quiet photograph}. A journalist asks what you regret.

outcomes.text: I named a war I should have stopped. The country went quiet and then forgave me.
I named it. The government's reaction was less forgiving.
It was the truth and it sounded like a lie. The headline was cruel.
It went down well. Apparently people like a monarch who doesn't blink.
I asked her what she regretted. It became the best interview of the year.
She said nothing, and the silence was long and mine.

title: A reign remembered
text: The history of the reign is being written by {~someone who never met you|someone who did|three people who disagree}. You are offered the chance to read it first.

choices.label: Read it and correct the facts

outcomes.text: I corrected eleven facts. The writer put them in a footnote.
I corrected the facts and found I had to correct the tone as well. It became a second book.
History is not mine to edit, only to deserve.
It came out flattering in the wrong places. The right places went unmentioned.
My memoir came out in the same month. Historians use both.
It was candid in ways I'd not intended. I was accused of vanity and then of honesty, and I'd rather the latter.

title: The first spell
text: {~The candle lit itself|The kettle boiled before you reached for it|A word you'd never said came out of your mouth}. Your {~grandmother|mother|neighbour} is watching you from the doorway.

outcomes.text: The second time was harder, and it worked. I felt something open a door in me.
The second time something broke. I swept up the pieces and said nothing.
She told me three things and refused to tell me the fourth. It was the right amount.
She laughed and told me I was late. I'd been late for years.
I pretended for a month. The candles pretended with me.
It didn't work. Things kept happening around me until I stopped pretending.

title: A circle of your own
text: {~Two women from the village|Three people you barely know|A stranger on the bus} have started leaving small things on your doorstep: a feather, a shell, a note that says 'when you're ready'.

outcomes.text: We cast a circle in my kitchen. The tea went cold and it was the best evening of the year.
One of them was an informer. I found out too late.
They were what they said they were. I let them wait until I was sure.
They gave up. I regretted my caution for a year.
I burned them and felt, briefly, safe. Then lonely.
The ashes spelled out something I didn't want to read.

title: The grimoire
text: You've reached the page of the book that {~was torn out|is written in a hand you recognise|is blank until you ask the right question}. The ink is {~damp|warm|still moving}.

outcomes.text: It was a recipe for something that cannot be named in a kitchen. It worked.
The room changed and so did I. I stopped being able to explain things to people who weren't there.

choices.label: Copy it into a safer hand

outcomes.text: It took a week. The copy was worse and kept me alive.
The copy had a mistake in it. Eventually I found where.
I closed it. It opened again when I left the room.
I closed it, and it let me. Some things can be put down.

title: Lanterns in the lane
text: {~A neighbour has been asking questions|The vicar called round without an excuse|A man with a notebook has been seen at the end of your road}. You realise you are not as invisible as you thought.

outcomes.text: It took an apple pie and a long conversation about nothing. They left feeling vaguely reassured.
It worked on one of them. The other noticed the pie wasn't quite natural.
I packed in a night and was gone before the milkman. I miss that garden.
The move saved me and cost me a friend who'd have followed.
It was either the bravest or the stupidest thing I've done. They did not come back.
It went terribly. It also went in the village's favour, which I hadn't counted on.

title: Mother of the coven
text: {~Someone's daughter|A woman half your age|A man who'd been a sceptic} has asked you to teach them. The coven is watching to see whether you'll say yes.

outcomes.text: It took years. They became better than me, and I was proud like a parent.
I taught too much too soon. Something went wrong and I carry it.
A careful curriculum, kindly given. Nobody was hurt, and nobody was great.
They found the rest elsewhere. I wasn't the only teacher after all.
The coven heard the refusal in silence. It was somebody else's turn.
A year later I changed my mind and found it was too late.

title: The first night out
text: {~A scream from an alley|A fire alarm three floors up|A car sliding on ice towards a crossing}. You are the only one near who can do something about it.

outcomes.text: It worked. I was home in time for the late news, and I couldn't sleep.
I did it, and someone filmed it. The footage was blurry and it was me.
Someone else handled it, badly. I told myself I'd learned something.
Nobody came. I'll carry that for a very long time.
In the confusion I took what I wanted. Nobody saw. I'd never felt so free.
It went wrong in a way that taught me what I was. I didn't like all of it.

title: An alias that sticks
text: A {~newspaper|blog|child} has started calling you by a name you didn't pick. {~It's not a good name.|It's better than yours.|It's catching on.}

outcomes.text: I redesigned the mask around it. By the end of the month it was on a lunchbox.
It stuck faster than I could shape it. I became someone I hadn't chosen to be.
They wrote the correction down. The new name sounded forced, and the old one stayed.
The correction became the story: the hero who didn't want a name.
A new name replaced it in a month. I was oddly relieved and oddly bereft.
It faded, and someone else wore it better. I watched from a rooftop.

title: Someone with the same gift
text: A figure {~watches you from the other side of a street|leaves a note on a rooftop|appears at the end of a night's work} with {~your powers, bent|a different idea of what they're for}. They've been following your work, and clearly disagree.

outcomes.text: It was a fight neither of us won. The city's windows will be repaired by spring.
They were better than I'd feared. I escaped, and the city knew something was wrong.
We talked until dawn. They didn't change their mind, and neither did I, but we'd both been listened to.
They used the conversation to learn my weakness. I only realised later.
They went away for a while. It's the kind of quiet that makes you check the rooftops.
They took it as an insult. It escalated, as these things do.

title: The mask slips
text: Someone {~in the crowd|at work|in your own family} looks at you for a beat too long. {~They know.|They're not sure.|They've decided to keep it to themselves.}

outcomes.text: They cried, laughed and asked a hundred questions. It was the best secret I've ever shared.
They told me they'd keep it, and a month later they told someone else.
I lied, and they let me. The lie held for a year.
I lied badly. They didn't say anything. They didn't have to.
A month on the road and nobody asked. When I came back, the question had gone.
The vanishing made it worse. Everyone has a theory.

title: A legend in the city
text: They're {~naming a bridge|painting a mural|writing a documentary} about you. {~Nobody's asked.|You're consulted, as a courtesy.}

outcomes.text: The mask came with me. I stood at the back and watched a child touch the paint.
I went, and someone recognised the way I stood. The next day the rumour was everywhere.
They changed the one detail I'd asked for. The rest is mine to live with.
They took it as a sign of modesty and put it in the caption.
Legends don't go to their own unveilings. It was probably right.
I stayed away and the city read it as a rebuke. The headline wasn't kind.
